title: What If a Hidden Ninth Planet Is Found Beyond Neptune?

scenes.text: What if a ninth planet is hiding past Neptune? Astronomers have been hunting for one since 2016.
Caltech astronomers noticed some icy objects in the Kuiper Belt have orbits that cluster together.
An unseen planet could explain it: about 5 to 10 times Earth's mass, and 20 to 30 times farther from the Sun than Neptune.
One lap around the Sun would take between 10,000 and 20,000 Earth years.
Keck and Subaru have searched without luck. Now the Rubin Observatory's 3,200 megapixel camera is looking, with an estimated 70 to 80 percent chance of finding it if it exists.
But some astronomers think the clustering is a statistical illusion. Either we find a ninth planet, or we learn the outer solar system is emptier than we thought.
